core_nodes.note_on_flux3: TextGenerate is what runs the prompt upsampler: it takes the upsampler loaded through CLIPLoader and produces the caption that CLIPTextEncode receives. None of the FLUX 3 nodes is a custom pack, which is why an installed FLUX 3 can look incomplete when it is not.

character_generator.note: Target for the character reference generator. Checked against a live instance on 2026-10-18: every role is installed, so the graph can be built and measured now. The repository on Hugging Face is access-gated, so downloads of anything else need an authenticated client.

roles.note: Quantisation variants of two checkpoints, base and step-distilled. One is enough. Grouped as alternatives on purpose: listing them flat made the checker report five files as missing when none were. Both spellings of the base int8 are listed because the upstream workflow omits the folder prefix while an install that keeps the file in a subfolder needs it -- the audit refuses the wrong one with value_not_in_list.

Writes the caption text in box mode, which is the refine step; Flux3BoxReconcileKJ then puts our ids back on the boxes it re-planned. It is NOT the conditioning encoder: wiring it to the sampler fails with a shape error (4096 against 20480). Not required for a plain text-to-image graph.

This is what feeds the sampler, loaded with CLIPLoader type flux3. Identified by scanning candidates with minimal real runs: the three 4B variants pass, the 8B VL and the 9B text models fail on a shape error. It is also what reads the reference images, so one file covers conditioning and references.
Shared with the FLUX 2 path; already there for the first-frame editor.

verified_combination.latent_and_scheduler: EmptyFlux2LatentImage + Flux2Scheduler -- FLUX 3 Klein has none of its own
verified_combination.evidence: 512x512, 2 steps, execution status success. The dry audit alone was not evidence: it validated the wiring while the encoder was still wrong.

character_generator.graph_note: The character sheet comes from Flux3PromptBuilderKJ: draw boxes on the output canvas, give each an id and a description, cite the id in the prompt, and it appends the boxes as a JSON table on a 0-1000 grid. Its references input grows with the number of references, so the count is not fixed. No latent trick is needed, unlike the FLUX 2 path, which required the enhancer pack to inject reference latents.
character_generator.upstream_workflows_note: Listed from the repository's file browser, which answers even on a gated repository. Their contents have not been read: an unauthenticated fetch returns the restriction notice instead of the file.
why_this_model: multi-reference generation is native: it takes several references and keeps characters recognisable across inputs, which is the character-sheet gesture
5.6B parameters, so a reference costs seconds rather than minutes
the same model does text-to-image, single-reference edit and multi-reference composition, so one graph covers the three things the character page needs
the layout builder that ships with it is a visual box editor, which is the interaction the character page wants anyway
